issues.legal_issue: A leasehold grant of public nazul land without public auction is valid only when good reason for departing from auction is established and recorded in writing.
material_facts: The State Government granted the plots without auction.
There was no evidence that the State Government recorded reasons in writing for dispensing with auction.
The Court was not satisfied that the State Government had good reason to dispense with auction.
issues.conclusion: The grant without auction was invalid and was rightly quashed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Rules 24 to 26, including Rule 26(1), leasehold rights in nazul land are generally to be disposed of by public auction. The State Government's authority under Rule 22 to dispose of plots without auction is controlled by Rule 26(1): good reason for departing from auction must exist, and the reasons must be recorded in writing. Both are essential prerequisites.

rule.if: public_land_allotment_challenged and lease_granted_without_auction and (not good_reason_for_no_auction or not reason_recorded_in_writing)

predicates.public_land_allotment_challenged: A proceeding challenges an allotment of public land.
predicates.lease_granted_without_auction: The authority granted leasehold rights in public land without holding a public auction.
predicates.good_reason_for_no_auction: The authority had a good reason for granting the land without auction.
predicates.reason_recorded_in_writing: The authority recorded in writing its reason for granting the land without auction.

issues.definition: When a challenged public-land allotment grants leasehold rights without auction and either there was no good reason or the reason was not recorded in writing, the grant is invalid.

issues.legal_issue: When the government reverses a policy that had made land unavailable for allotment, it must consider all eligible pending claims or invite fresh applications before selecting an allottee.
material_facts: The State Government had rejected all applications under a policy decision not to allot the land to displaced persons, rather than on the merits of the applications.
The State Government later reversed that policy and allotted plots to the appellants without considering the other applicants' claims.
The respondents and other claimants had also applied for plots.
The appellants' pursuit of review did not make them a separate class entitled to exclusive consideration after the policy changed.
issues.conclusion: The State Government could not allot the plots to the appellants in disregard of the other claims; it had to reconsider the existing applications or invite fresh applications.
issues.legal_principle: A government decision reversing a policy that had made land unavailable for allotment reopens the opportunity to all claimants. The government must reconsider pending applications or notify that the land is available and invite fresh applications; it cannot select one applicant while disregarding other claims. The Court treated the reversal and the subsequent allotment as a composite decision and rejected the argument that only applicants who pursued review could benefit from the policy change.

rule.if: public_land_allotment_proceeding and land_reopened_for_allotment and applications_rejected_only_because_land_was_unavailable and competing_claims_exist and allotment_made_without_reconsidering_claims_or_inviting_applications

predicates.public_land_allotment_proceeding: The proceeding concerns the government's allotment of public land.
predicates.land_reopened_for_allotment: The government changed its policy and made land previously unavailable open to allotment.
predicates.applications_rejected_only_because_land_: The government rejected applications because its policy made the land unavailable, not because it assessed the applicants' merits.
predicates.competing_claims_exist: Other applicants had also claimed the land.
predicates.allotment_made_without_reconsidering_cla: The government allotted the land without reconsidering pending claims or inviting fresh applications.

issues.definition: When land is reopened for allotment after applications were rejected only because it was unavailable, and competing claims exist, an allotment made without reconsidering those claims or inviting applications requires that the competing claims be considered.

issues.legal_issue: A disposal of state land in Bhumidhari rights at a premium based on market value, rather than on favourable terms, is a disposal under the general land-disposal provision and not the favourable-terms exception.
material_facts: The plots were disposed of in Bhumidhari rights.
The premium was fixed by reference to the plots' market value.
The grant was not made to the appellants on favourable terms.
issues.conclusion: The grant was not attributable to the favourable-terms exception and was intended to be made under the general land-disposal provision.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 149(1) of the Madhya Pradesh Land Revenue Code, state land, subject to applicable rules, may be disposed of in Bhumidhari or Bhumiswami rights. The Court held that this grant did not fall within the exception in Section 149(2)(c) for land given on favourable terms for specified purposes because the plots were granted in Bhumidhari rights at a premium based on market value.

rule.if: state_land_grant_classification_proceeding and land_disposed_in_bhumidhari_rights and premium_based_on_market_value and grant_not_on_favourable_terms

predicates.state_land_grant_classification_proceedi: The proceeding requires the legal classification of a grant of state land.
predicates.land_disposed_in_bhumidhari_rights: The state disposed of the land in Bhumidhari rights.
predicates.premium_based_on_market_value: The premium for the land was based on its market value.
predicates.grant_not_on_favourable_terms: The state did not grant the land on favourable terms to the allottee.

issues.definition: When state land is disposed of in Bhumidhari rights at a market-value-based premium and not on favourable terms, the grant falls under the general land-disposal category.
